## Step 1: Define and Resolve the Workspace, Source, and Destination Paths

```powershell
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

$workspace    = 'C:\Work\MyProject'
$sourceName   = 'OldData'
$destParent   = 'C:\Work\MyProject\Archive'

$workspacePath = (Resolve-Path -LiteralPath $workspace).Path
$sourcePath    = (Resolve-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $workspacePath $sourceName)).Path
$destParentPath = (Resolve-Path -LiteralPath $destParent).Path
```

`Resolve-Path` is called with `-LiteralPath` so wildcard characters in names are never interpreted as patterns. If any path fails to resolve, the cmdlet throws a non-terminating error that `$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'` promotes to terminating, halting the script before any mutation occurs. Note that `Resolve-Path` on the destination parent requires it to already exist; if the destination parent must be created, do so explicitly with `New-Item -ItemType Directory` before this step and re-resolve.

## Step 2: Verify All Paths Are Contained Within the Workspace

```powershell
function Test-PathInsideWorkspace {
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Path,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Workspace
    )
    $fullPath     = [System.IO.Path]::GetFullPath($Path)
    $fullWorkspace = [System.IO.Path]::GetFullPath($Workspace)

    if ($fullPath -eq $fullWorkspace) { return $true }

    return $fullPath.StartsWith(
        $fullWorkspace.TrimEnd('\') + '\',
        [System.StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase
    )
}

if (-not (Test-PathInsideWorkspace -Path $sourcePath     -Workspace $workspacePath) -or
    -not (Test-PathInsideWorkspace -Path $destParentPath -Workspace $workspacePath)) {
    throw "Path validation failed: source or destination escapes the workspace."
}
```

The containment check appends a trailing separator before `StartsWith` so that a sibling directory like `C:\Work\MyProjectArchive` cannot pass as being inside `C:\Work\MyProject`. The workspace itself is allowed as an exact match. This is the fail-closed gate: any ambiguity, symlink redirection, or unexpected resolution result causes the script to throw rather than proceed.

## Step 3: Confirm the Destination Does Not Already Exist

```powershell
$destPath = Join-Path $destParentPath $sourceName

if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $destPath) {
    throw "Destination '$destPath' already exists. Refusing to overwrite or merge."
}
```

`Move-Item` behavior when the destination exists is inconsistent across providers and can merge or overwrite depending on the situation. Fail-closed design demands refusing to proceed rather than guessing intent. `Test-Path -LiteralPath` again avoids wildcard interpretation.

## Step 4: Enumerate and Snapshot the Source Contents (Read-Only Safety Check)

```powershell
$sourceItems = Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $sourcePath -Recurse -Force

Write-Host "Moving '$sourcePath' ($($sourceItems.Count) items) to '$destPath'"

# Optional: verify no unexpected top-level entries exist that suggest the
# wrong directory was resolved
$topLevel = Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $sourcePath -Force
$topLevel | ForEach-Object { Write-Host "  - $($_.Name)" }
```

This step is deliberately read-only. It produces an inventory that can be logged or compared after the move, and it gives the operator a final visible confirmation of what is about to be relocated. Because nothing has been mutated yet, any abort here is consequence-free. Unrelated files elsewhere in the workspace are untouched by definition — nothing outside `$sourcePath` is read for modification purposes.

```powershell
Move-Item -LiteralPath $sourcePath -Destination $destPath

if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $destPath) -or (Test-Path -LiteralPath $sourcePath)) {
    throw "Move verification failed: destination missing or source still present."
}

$movedItems = Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $destPath -Recurse -Force
if ($movedItems.Count -ne $sourceItems.Count) {
    throw "Item count mismatch after move: expected $($sourceItems.Count), found $($movedItems.Count)."
}

```

The move itself uses `Move-Item -LiteralPath` for the source, which guarantees the explicitly named directory is moved without wildcard expansion. On the same volume this is a metadata rename (fast, atomic at the directory level); across volumes it becomes a copy-then-delete, which is why the post-move verification — destination exists, source is gone, item counts match — matters. If verification fails, the script throws, leaving the state visible for manual recovery rather than silently continuing.
